source_refs.consumption_role: Owns the Phase 7 DataHub guardrails and now routes this local resource budget as a Phase 7c precondition.
Defines provider drift and no-silent-default requirements that DataHub jobs must preserve without default full-system refreshes.
Defines market and bucket separation; local execution defaults mirror that separation instead of mixing all lanes by default.
Tracks SR-RESOURCE-001 until future DataHub / runner implementation enforces this contract in code.

budget_profiles.role: Default mode for a local desktop run, review slice, or single lane evidence task.
notes: A normal run should target one market, one lane, one bounded as-of or date window, and one artifact family.
A runner must reuse reviewed local caches when available instead of defaulting to full refresh.
This profile is sufficient for ordinary manual analysis because the user does not need all four systems to run at once.

budget_profiles.role: Optional mode for a future batch job that intentionally broadens scope after separate review.
notes: A heavy profile still does not authorize provider calls, full-market download, DataHub implementation, or all-system parallel execution.
Future heavy jobs must declare expected row counts, output size, cache impact, checkpoint path, and abort / resume behavior before execution.
If a future task really needs all markets or all lanes, it requires a separate explicit user approval and reviewed job spec.

implementation_gates.required_resolution: Every future DataHub / runner job spec must validate against schemas/datahub_job_spec.schema.json and declare budget_profile, market, lane, as_of or date_window, expected inputs, expected outputs, cache policy, and abort policy.
DataHub reads must be partitionable by market, lane, as_of_date, date_window, provider_family, and artifact_type before production-like use.
Future factor and report paths must lazy-load required fields and materialize only the requested slice, not all four systems.
Longer jobs must be resumable and idempotent, with checkpoints or cache manifests that prevent starting over after a local interruption.
Any future all-market, all-lane, full-refresh, or high-output batch run must be separately approved by the user and reviewed as its own job spec.

limitations: This contract is a design boundary only; it does not benchmark the user's machine or measure actual CPU, memory, disk, or runtime.
It does not implement DataHub, adapters, runner enforcement, provider access, or cache writers.
It does not resolve SR-PROVIDER-001 and does not authorize Phase 7c implementation.
Future implementation must add code-level enforcement and tests before this risk can be closed.
